audit_findings.title: Current shares may be paired with a stale interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.4 million pre-tax H1 2026 year-over-year interest-expense increase; $6.6 million pre-tax annualized increase over FY2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher current interest expense reduces equity-level OE retained in the DCF; debt-funded repurchases simultaneously reduce the share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had outstanding borrowings of $ 272.5 million under our revolving credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated. H1 2026 interest expense was $9.6 million versus $6.2 million in H1 2025, while June debt reached $358.9 million. Annualizing H1 2026 interest expense gives $19.2 million, $6.6 million above FY2025's $12.6 million and equal to 26% of the $25.4 million OE anchor before tax effects. That is capable of materially lowering the per-share valuation despite the reduced share count.
audit_findings.action: Normalize annual interest expense using June debt, the $120 million swaps, cross-currency hedge effects and commitment fees; determine how much incremental borrowing funded repurchases; then rerun OE and all scenarios using the current fully diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: Brain Corp securities are absent from the stated perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.3 million June 2026 carrying value and $0.5 million H1 2026 equity-method loss
audit_findings.mechanism: A non-operating classification would add the securities to the equity bridge and purge investee results from OE; an operating classification would retain investee results in OE without a separate bridge addition.
audit_findings.evidence: The investment consists of $ 12.1 million of redeemable convertible preferred stock, $ 12.2 million of non-redeemable convertible preferred stock, and $ 7.8 million of warrants.
audit_findings.explanation: The zero-stake bridge omits a demonstrated $11.8 million debt security and $19.5 million equity-method investment. Adding the entire $31.3 million carrying value would raise base equity value by 7.2%, or about $1.75 per share, from $24.25 to about $26.00—still far below the $71.97 market price. The recorded H1 loss was only $0.5 million. Larger future losses remain possible but are not established by the record.
audit_findings.action: Designate Brain explicitly as operating or non-operating, obtain current carrying values and investee results, and rerun the bridge and OE consistently; monitor subsequent losses and impairments for a change in scale.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized ERP spending may evade the reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.1 million net asset increase; cash paid unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cloud-implementation cash spending should reduce OE as required reinvestment if it is not already captured; treating temporary rollout spending as perpetual maintenance would instead depress normalized OE and growth economics.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had capitalized implementation costs, net of amortization, of $53.4 million and $23.3 million, respectively, included in other assets within the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization is demonstrated, but omission from OE is not: the record does not show whether cash implementation payments were captured outside property-and-equipment capex. The net ERP asset increased $30.1 million, exceeding the $25.4 million anchor, so a missed deduction is reasonably capable of changing the valuation. The recurring maintenance portion and actual cash paid are unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace cloud-implementation payments through the cash-flow working-capital and other-assets lines and the OE worksheet, identify additions net of noncash movements, prevent double counting, and rerun scenarios using separately supported rollout and steady-state maintenance amounts.

audit_findings.title: The appealed judgment needs explicit one-time claim treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.9 million computed June 2026 accrued claim; $6.0 million FY2025 pre-tax charge
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-time earnings charge affects the OE anchor, while the accrued cash obligation belongs in the equity bridge if the charge is normalized out; recording both or neither misstates value.
audit_findings.evidence: The bond secures payment of the judgment, including applicable post-judgment interest and costs, if the judgment is affirmed or otherwise becomes payable following the appeal.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and anchor charge are demonstrated, but the valuation worksheet does not reveal whether an add-back occurred. Deducting the full $20.9 million claim alone would reduce base value by 4.8%, or about $1.17 per share. Illustratively, adding back the $6.0 million charge after the FY2025 24.3% tax rate and capitalizing it at the base operating-PV-to-anchor ratio, then deducting $20.9 million, produces an approximately $42.9 million net increase, or about $2.40 per share. Neither treatment closes the gap to the $71.97 price, although exact-once treatment remains necessary.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $20.9 million computed June accrual, the $6.0 million FY2025 charge, the $0.4 million H1 2026 interest accrual and every OE adjustment; rerun with the recurring charge removed and the expected cash claim deducted exactly once.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 anchor embeds a demonstrably temporary operational shock
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary lost contribution margin and stabilization costs depress the OE anchor that is compounded through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The system transition also resulted in the loss of three weeks of machine order entry and parts shipping capability, as well as contributing to slower transaction processing and prolonged customer delays.
audit_findings.explanation: The three-week shutdown and related disruption are demonstrated, but their contribution to the $81.2 million OE decline from 2024 is not quantified. The record also shows softer demand and continuing ERP-related constraints, with H1 2026 operating income falling to $20.8 million from $50.2 million and net income to $7.8 million from $33.3 million. A material normalization could change value, but current evidence cannot separate temporary effects from persistent operating weakness.
audit_findings.action: Use monthly 2025-2026 orders, shipments, backlog conversion, gross margin, recovery labor, technology support and other stabilization costs to quantify the temporary component; rerun only after actual recovery supports an add-back and exclude recurring ERP support and transformation spending.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not all be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $76.9 million maximum bridge exposure, equal to about $4.30 per share and 17.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any restricted, trapped or operationally necessary cash must be excluded from the surplus-cash equity bridge or reduced for repatriation costs.
audit_findings.evidence: In general, it is our practice and intention to permanently reinvest the earnings of our foreign subsidiaries and repatriate earnings only when the tax impact is zero or immaterial.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a foreign-reinvestment policy but does not establish that any specified part of June cash is inaccessible or required. Even removing the entire $76.9 million balance would lower base value from $24.25 to about $19.95 per share and bull value from $26.58 to about $22.28, both still far below the $71.97 market price. Therefore the maximum possible adjustment from this bridge line does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June cash balance by legal entity and jurisdiction, identify restricted cash, minimum operating cash and repatriation taxes, and replace the face-value bridge addition with documented distributable surplus.
